Monthly Program Report - Cascadia Freight Fleet Telematics Rollout
Month: February | Sponsor: Tariq Hassan | Program Lead: Beatriz Souza

Executive summary
The telematics hardware rollout across Cascadia's 1,200-truck fleet is 65% complete (780 trucks), on pace for the planned April 30 completion.

Installation progress
- Pacific region: 310 of 320 trucks complete (97%)
- Mountain region: 280 of 350 trucks complete (80%)
- Central region: 190 of 530 trucks complete (36%) - behind pace due to a parts shortage described below

Parts shortage
The GPS antenna model specified for this rollout has a 6-week backorder from the manufacturer, first reported Jan 15. Pacific and Mountain regions had already stocked enough units before the shortage hit; Central region had not, which explains its lower completion rate. A substitute antenna model has been qualified as of Feb 20 and Central region installations resume at full pace this week.

Budget
Approved budget: $3.6M. Spend to date: $2.1M. The parts shortage has not increased per-unit cost - the substitute antenna is priced the same as the original - but it has pushed roughly $400K of planned February spend into March as installations slipped.

Driver feedback
A survey of 150 drivers with the new system installed found 82% reported the new fuel-efficiency coaching feature 'somewhat' or 'very' useful. The remaining 18% cited the in-cab alert sound as too frequent; a software update reducing alert frequency ships March 5.

Safety metrics
Hard-braking events per 1,000 miles dropped 22% fleet-wide among trucks with telematics installed for at least 30 days, compared to a control group of not-yet-installed trucks over the same period.

Risks
1. (Medium) If the substitute antenna reveals any unforeseen compatibility issue at scale, Central region could fall further behind; the team is monitoring the first 50 substitute installations closely before scaling up.
2. (Low) Driver survey response rate was only 12.5% (150 of 1,200); results should be treated as directional, not conclusive, until a larger sample is collected at the 90-day mark.

Next steps
Beatriz to report Central region's substitute-antenna install rate weekly through March. Tariq to review the shifted March budget with Finance.

Vendor note
The antenna manufacturer has confirmed the original model's backorder will clear by late March, but the team plans to continue with the substitute model for the remainder of the rollout regardless, since qualifying a second supplier reduces future single-vendor risk. This decision was made jointly by Beatriz and Tariq after the Feb 20 qualification results came back clean.

state:
Vendor Evaluation Call - Driftwood Airlines Crew Scheduling
Rep: Dmitri Volkov | Feb 25

Dmitri: Thanks for the time. Last we spoke you were also considering building this in-house. Where does that stand?

Contact (Julia Castellano, VP Operations, Driftwood Airlines): We got a rough estimate from our engineering team - 14 months and roughly $1.8M fully loaded, mostly because crew-scheduling rules for airlines are genuinely complex with FAA rest-time rules.

Dmitri: How does that compare to what you're seeing from vendors like us?

Julia: Your quote is $420,000/year, and a competitor, a company called Skyframe Systems, quoted $380,000/year. Both are obviously cheaper than building it ourselves over any reasonable timeframe, so build-vs-buy isn't really the live question anymore. It's you versus Skyframe.

Dmitri: Understood. Can I ask what's driving the gap toward Skyframe on price?

Julia: Skyframe's price is lower, but they've never implemented for an airline our size - their biggest customer is a regional carrier with 40 aircraft, we have 210. You've done three airlines our size or larger, which matters more to us than the $40,000/year difference.

Dmitri: That's helpful context. Is there anything Skyframe offers that we don't, that's swaying things their way?

Julia: Not that I've seen. If anything, our ops team found their demo less polished. I want to be honest with you though - our CFO looks at the raw number first, so you may need to help me build the case for the experience premium being worth $40K/year.

Dmitri: Understood, I can put together a one-pager quantifying implementation risk for a carrier our size versus Skyframe's track record. Would a reference call with one of our similar-sized airline customers help?

Julia: Yes, that would help a lot with the CFO conversation specifically.

Dmitri: I'll set that up this week. To confirm - building in-house is off the table at this point?

Julia: Correct, off the table. Timeline alone rules it out even before cost - 14 months is too slow regardless of price.

Dmitri: One more thing - what's your internal timeline for a decision, so I know how to pace the reference call and one-pager?

Julia: We'd like to decide by the end of March, ideally, so our new scheduling process is live well before next winter's peak season.

Action items: Dmitri to arrange a reference call with a comparable airline customer by March 3. Dmitri to send a one-pager on implementation risk at scale.

Kestrel Media Platform - Changelog v11.0 through v11.3

v11.0 (Mar 10)
- New: Multi-author collaboration on drafts (up to 5 simultaneous editors, up from 1).
- New: Analytics dashboard adds a 'read completion rate' metric alongside existing pageviews.
- Breaking: The /v1/articles endpoint's author field (a single string) is replaced by an authors array. Integrations reading the old author field will get an empty value, not an error - this is a silent breaking change with no exceptions.

v11.1 (Mar 24)
- Fixed: Read-completion-rate metric undercounted for articles with embedded video, since video-heavy scroll behavior wasn't accounted for; now corrected.
- New: Draft version history now retains 90 days of history, up from 30 days, for all tiers including Free.

v11.2 (Apr 7)
- New: Scheduled publishing can now target a specific timezone per article, instead of always using account-default timezone.
- Fixed: Multi-author collaboration occasionally showed a stale cursor position for the second editor; now syncs in real time.

v11.3 (Apr 21)
- Breaking: Free tier's draft version history retention is reduced back to 30 days (the 90-day retention introduced in v11.1 is now Pro-tier and above only). Free-tier drafts older than 30 days as of this release are not retroactively deleted, but new drafts follow the 30-day limit.
- New: Multi-author collaboration limit raised from 5 to 10 simultaneous editors for Enterprise tier only; other tiers remain at 5.
- Deprecated: The legacy /v1/articles author string field entirely stops being populated (previously it silently returned empty; now it's removed from the response object). Use authors.

Known issues (as of v11.3)
- A handful of Enterprise customers report the 10-editor collaboration limit isn't yet reflected in their account settings UI, though it works correctly when tested directly; a UI fix is planned for v11.4.

Migration guide
Any integration still reading the author string field must migrate to authors - this became silently empty in v11.0 and is fully removed as of v11.3. Free-tier customers relying on 90-day draft history should note the reduction back to 30 days in v11.3, though nothing already older than 30 days was deleted retroactively.

Support notes
Most v11.0 migration tickets were about the author field change; support reports the silent-empty behavior caused more confusion than a hard error would have, since integrations didn't immediately notice anything was wrong. Support now recommends Kestrel flag silent-empty breaking changes more prominently and more loudly in future release notes going forward.

Incident Summary - Duplicate Tracking Numbers, Ironbridge Logistics Platform
Date: Mar 8 | Severity: SEV-2

A counter-reset bug in the tracking-number generator caused 62 shipments to be assigned tracking numbers that were already in use by other active shipments, between 02:00 and 02:40 UTC.

Impact: Customers looking up one of the 62 duplicated numbers saw the wrong shipment's status for up to 6 hours before the issue was caught by a customer service escalation, not automated monitoring.

Root cause: A database failover at 01:58 UTC caused the tracking-number counter (an in-memory value) to reset to its last-checkpointed value instead of its true last-issued value, a gap of about 400 numbers that then got reissued.

Fix: Counter now persists on every increment instead of periodic checkpoints; failover-safe as of Mar 9 deploy.

Incident Summary - Firmware Rollback, Quicksilver Robotics Fleet
Date: Mar 12 | Severity: SEV-2

Firmware v8.4, deployed to 300 warehouse robots starting Mar 10, caused a navigation bug where robots occasionally paused for 30-60 seconds at intersections with no obstacle present, reducing fleet throughput by roughly 9% over two days before the pattern was identified.

The bug was traced to an overly conservative update to the obstacle-prediction model, intended to reduce collision risk but tuned too aggressively, causing false-positive obstacle detections at intersections specifically.

All 300 robots were rolled back to firmware v8.3 by Mar 12, 18:00, restoring normal throughput. A corrected v8.5 with a properly tuned model is in testing, targeting re-deployment the week of Mar 24.

No collisions or safety incidents occurred during the affected period - the bug caused overly cautious behavior, not unsafe behavior.

state:
Postmortem: Appointment Scheduling System Outage
Incident ID: INC-771 | Solace Health Platform | Date: Mar 15
Authors: Aleksander Brandt, Simone Laurent

Summary
Between 07:00 and 09:15 UTC, the patient-facing appointment scheduling system was completely unavailable, returning connection errors for all requests. Phone-based scheduling (a separate system operated by clinic staff) was unaffected and used as a fallback.

Timeline
- 06:55 - A routine database maintenance window begins, expected to take 10 minutes with no downtime (online index rebuild).
- 07:00 - The index rebuild unexpectedly takes an exclusive lock on the appointments table, blocking all reads and writes.
- 07:02 - Scheduling system starts returning connection timeout errors as requests queue behind the lock.
- 07:05 - On-call engineer Simone Laurent is paged.
- 07:10 - Simone's initial hypothesis: an application-layer bug, since the maintenance window was expected to be non-blocking.
- 07:25 - Simone escalates to Aleksander Brandt after ruling out an application-layer cause.
- 07:40 - Aleksander identifies the database lock and determines the index rebuild's "online" mode silently fell back to a blocking mode because the appointments table exceeded a size threshold undocumented in the database vendor's tooling.
- 08:00 - Killing the rebuild job is considered but rejected, since partially-built indexes could leave the table in a worse state; the team decides to let it complete instead.
- 09:15 - The rebuild completes; the lock releases; scheduling system recovers immediately with no further errors.

Root cause
An index rebuild tool's "online" mode silently used a blocking strategy once the table exceeded an undocumented size threshold, and no monitoring existed to detect a long-held table lock in progress.

Impact
Patients could not book, reschedule, or cancel appointments online for 2 hours and 15 minutes. Clinic staff fielded an estimated 340 phone calls during this window, roughly triple the normal volume, but no appointments were missed or lost - phone scheduling covered all requests, just with longer hold times.

Action items
1. Add monitoring for long-held table locks with automatic paging - owner: Aleksander, due Mar 22.
2. Test index rebuilds against a production-sized table copy before running on production going forward - owner: Simone, due Mar 29.
3. Document the vendor's undocumented size threshold internally and file a bug report with the vendor - owner: Aleksander, due Mar 20.

What went well
Phone scheduling as a fallback meant zero missed appointments despite the 2+ hour online outage.

state:
Quarterly Report - Marigold Finance Core Ledger Migration
Q1 | Sponsor: Rowan Blackwood | PM: Ivy Sorensen

Executive summary
The core ledger migration to the new platform remains on track for the June 30 cutover. Parallel-run testing (old and new systems processing the same transactions side by side) began Feb 1.

Parallel-run results
Through March, 340,000 transactions have been processed in parallel. 339,650 matched exactly between old and new systems (99.9%). The 350 mismatches were all traced to a rounding-rule difference in fee calculations for a specific account type (business overdraft accounts), which affects roughly 2% of the customer base.

Fee rounding fix
Engineering has identified the fix: the new system needs to match the old system's round-half-up behavior for this account type specifically, rather than the new system's default round-half-even behavior. Fix is coded and in testing, targeting deployment by Apr 15, well before the June 30 cutover.

Budget
Approved budget: $5.2M over 14 months. Spend to date: $3.4M, on track against a $3.5M planned-to-date figure.

Risk register
1. (High) If the rounding fix introduces any new discrepancy class, the parallel-run clock effectively restarts for affected account types, which could threaten the June 30 date. Mitigation: fix is being tested against 3 months of historical overdraft-account transactions before redeployment to parallel-run.
2. (Medium) Regulatory sign-off is required before cutover; the regulator has requested the parallel-run achieve 99.95% match rate (not yet met) sustained for 60 consecutive days before they'll review the cutover request.
3. (Low) Two engineers rotating off the project in April for a prior commitment; backfill hiring is in progress and not yet a blocker.

Compliance note
The 99.95% regulatory threshold is stricter than the team's own internal target of 99.9%, which has already been met. Reaching 99.95% specifically requires resolving the rounding-rule mismatches described above.

Next steps
Ivy to deploy the rounding fix by Apr 15 and restart the 60-day sustained-match clock immediately after. Rowan to brief the board that June 30 depends on hitting 99.95% by roughly May 1 to leave room for the regulator's review window.

Stakeholder note
The regulator's account team has been briefed informally on the rounding-rule fix and did not raise concerns about the approach, though their formal review only happens once the 60-day sustained window is complete. Ivy plans a follow-up briefing once the fix is live in parallel-run, well ahead of the formal 60-day clock restarting for the affected account types.

Vendor Call - Cinderpath Games Customer Support Tooling
Rep: Fatou Diallo | Mar 25

Fatou: Thanks for joining. Last time we spoke, support tickets were split between email and your in-game contact form. Any change there?

Contact (Theo Marchetti, Head of Player Support, Cinderpath Games): Volume's up 30% since our last conversation, mostly because of the new title launch. We're now genuinely underwater without something better than spreadsheet-based triage.

Fatou: Understood. Where are you in evaluating us versus alternatives?

Theo: We looked at two others. One, called HelpAnchor, we ruled out - it doesn't support in-game contact form ingestion, only email, and that's half our volume. The other, Support Nest, is still in the running alongside you.

Fatou: What's the comparison looking like against Support Nest?

Theo: Feature-wise, close. Support Nest is slightly cheaper - $2,400/month versus your $2,900/month for our ticket volume tier. But their onboarding timeline is 6 weeks versus your 2 weeks, and with ticket volume where it is, the faster onboarding might be worth more than the price gap.

Fatou: That's helpful. Is pricing or onboarding speed the bigger factor for your decision right now?

Theo: Honestly, onboarding speed, given where we are. I need to be upfront though - our CFO, who I don't have on these calls, ultimately has to approve anything over $2,500/month, so your price point specifically needs her sign-off, where Support Nest's wouldn't.

Fatou: Got it, that's useful to know for how we structure a proposal. Would a shorter initial commitment help get CFO approval, even at the higher monthly rate?

Theo: Possibly - if you could do a 3-month pilot at a lower rate before the full commitment, that removes some of the CFO's risk concern, since it's a smaller number to approve initially.

Fatou: Let me see what I can put together on that structure. One more question - is there a hard deadline driving this decision?

Theo: Not a hard deadline, but every week on the current setup means a growing ticket backlog, so sooner is meaningfully better than later for us, even without a specific date.

Fatou: Understood. Last thing - who else, besides you and the CFO, would be part of a final decision?

Theo: Just us two, really. I own the tool selection technically, she owns the budget sign-off. No committee beyond that.

Action items: Fatou to propose a 3-month pilot structure to ease CFO approval. Theo to share updated ticket volume numbers for accurate pricing.

Quicksilver Robotics Fleet Manager - Changelog v3.0 to v3.2

v3.0 (Apr 1)
- New: Real-time battery-health prediction, flagging robots likely to need battery service within 2 weeks.
- New: Fleet-wide firmware rollout can now be staged (10% / 50% / 100%) instead of all-at-once.
- Breaking: The /v1/robots/{id}/status endpoint's battery_pct field is renamed to battery_percent; battery_pct is removed entirely, not aliased. Integrations must update immediately upon upgrading to v3.0.

v3.1 (Apr 15)
- Fixed: Staged rollouts occasionally skipped the 50% stage and jumped from 10% to 100% if triggered too quickly in succession; a minimum 1-hour gap between stages is now enforced.
- New: Battery-health prediction accuracy improved; false-positive rate (flagging healthy batteries) dropped from 12% to 4% based on internal validation.

v3.2 (Apr 29)
- New: Geofencing alerts can now trigger a webhook in addition to the in-app notification.
- Fixed: A memory leak in the fleet-map rendering view that caused the operator dashboard to slow down after several hours of continuous use.
- Deprecated: The /v1/fleet/summary endpoint's legacy_format=true query parameter; the legacy format will stop being supported in v4.0, with no announced date yet for v4.0.

Known issues (as of v3.2)
- A subset of customers on the staged-rollout feature report the 1-hour minimum gap (from v3.1) is longer than they'd like for urgent security patches; an "emergency rollout" override is being considered for a future release, not yet built. Product has not committed to a timeline for this override yet, pending further customer feedback on how common the urgent-patch scenario really is.

Migration guide
Any integration reading battery_pct broke immediately upon upgrading to v3.0 and must switch to battery_percent - there was no transition period for this specific field. The legacy_format parameter on /v1/fleet/summary still works as of v3.2 and will continue to until v4.0 ships, which has no announced date.

Support notes
Support reports the battery_pct rename generated a spike in urgent tickets immediately after v3.0 shipped, since it broke integrations with no warning period, unlike most of Quicksilver's other breaking changes which typically include a deprecation window. Support has asked the API team to commit to a standard deprecation window for all future breaking changes, and the team has tentatively agreed for releases after v3.2. Customers who filed urgent tickets over the battery_pct rename have all been individually followed up with by support this month to confirm their integrations are now fully stable on the new battery_percent field going forward, with no remaining open tickets on that issue as of this week's support queue review.

PORTSIDE — A fire tore through a storage warehouse at the Portside Cannery late Thursday night, causing what officials estimate could be more than $2 million in damage, though no injuries were reported.

The fire was first reported at 11:42 p.m. by a security guard who noticed smoke near the loading dock on the building's east side. More than 40 firefighters from three surrounding districts responded, and the blaze was brought under control by 3:15 a.m. Friday, according to Fire Chief Mara Oduya.

“At this point we have no reason to believe this was arson,” Oduya said at a morning briefing. “Investigators are looking closely at an electrical panel near where the fire appears to have started, but it's too early to name a definitive cause.”

The cannery, which employs about 120 workers, was closed for the overnight shift when the fire broke out, and plant manager Devon Track said all staff were accounted for. Production is expected to resume within the week once inspectors clear the undamaged sections of the plant.

The warehouse sits adjacent to a seafood storage facility operated by Bayline Seafood, a separate company that leases space in the same industrial park. Bayline said its facility sustained only minor smoke damage and remained operational Friday morning.

Thursday's fire is the second at the industrial park in two years; a 2024 blaze destroyed a textile warehouse two lots away, a fire that investigators later attributed to a faulty forklift battery charger. Chief Oduya said there is no indication the two incidents are related.

Local business owners near the industrial park said they were relieved the fire did not spread further. “We could see the glow from three blocks away,” said Priya Nandan, who owns a diner across the street and stayed open through the night to give firefighters coffee.

The Portside Fire Department said a full incident report would be released within 30 days, standard for fires of this size, and that the state fire marshal's office has been notified given the estimated dollar value of the damage, though such notification does not by itself indicate any suspicion of wrongdoing.

The Portside City Council, which oversees fire-code inspections for the industrial park, confirmed the park had passed its most recent inspection in March and said it had no immediate plans to order additional inspections of the remaining tenants. Chief Oduya added that residents within a two-block radius reported no smoke-related health complaints as of Friday morning.

Portside Cannery's parent company, Coastal Provisions Inc., said in a statement that it carries insurance covering both property damage and business interruption, and that it does not expect the fire to affect its ability to fulfill existing orders.

notes: Stated in the first sentence.

state: Preliminary Results of a Phase II Trial of Odarafenib in Advanced Melanoma. In this open-label Phase II trial, 84 patients with unresectable stage III or IV melanoma received odarafenib 200 mg twice daily. At a median follow-up of 11 months, the objective response rate was 34% (95% CI, 24–45%), and median progression-free survival was 7.2 months. Technical Report: Evaluating FalconNet and OrcaNet on the MERIT Benchmark.

We evaluate two recent vision-language models, FalconNet-7B and OrcaNet-13B, on the MERIT benchmark, a suite of eight tasks spanning visual question answering, chart reasoning, and document understanding. All models are evaluated zero-shot, with no task-specific fine-tuning.

On the aggregate MERIT score, OrcaNet-13B achieves 61.4 points, compared to 58.9 for FalconNet-7B. However, the gap is not uniform across tasks. On the chart-reasoning subset, FalconNet-7B scores 52.3, outperforming OrcaNet-13B's 49.1, which we attribute to FalconNet's dedicated chart-pretraining stage. On document understanding, OrcaNet-13B leads by a wider margin, 71.0 versus 60.7.

We also compare inference latency: FalconNet-7B, being roughly half the parameter count, runs at 340 ms per query on our reference A100 setup, versus 610 ms for OrcaNet-13B.

For context, we note that a third model, PelicanVL-3B, was evaluated in a prior study (Ibarra et al., 2025) on a different, non-public benchmark, and is not directly comparable to the results here; we do not evaluate PelicanVL-3B in this work.

Both models show substantial weaknesses on the spatial-reasoning subset, scoring below 40 points, which we interpret as evidence that neither architecture has solved fine-grained spatial grounding. We caution that our results are based on a single evaluation run per model and may not capture the full variance of these benchmarks; a more thorough study with multiple seeds is left to future work.

Overall, these preliminary results suggest OrcaNet-13B may be preferable for document-heavy applications, while FalconNet-7B's lower latency and competitive chart-reasoning performance could make it attractive for latency-sensitive deployments.

The MERIT benchmark's eight tasks are drawn from a mix of publicly released datasets and a held-out set of 1,200 newly collected question-answer pairs designed to reduce the risk of training-data contamination. Each task contributes equally to the aggregate score regardless of the number of examples it contains.

A qualitative error analysis of 50 randomly sampled failures from each model suggests that FalconNet-7B's errors on document-understanding tasks are concentrated in multi-column layouts and dense tables, while OrcaNet-13B's chart-reasoning errors more often involve misreading axis labels rather than misunderstanding the underlying trend. We did not perform a similar qualitative analysis for the spatial-reasoning subset, which we leave to future work alongside the multi-seed evaluation. All code and evaluation prompts used in this report are being prepared for release alongside the camera-ready version of the paper.

state: A survey of the dwarf galaxy NGC 5253-B using the Alden Radio Array has detected an unusual radio pulse train recurring every 4.6 hours, a pattern the authors say may indicate a previously uncatalogued magnetar, though they note that instrumental artifacts have not been fully ruled out. Follow-up observations are scheduled for early next year to confirm the periodicity and rule out terrestrial interference. The authors emphasize that, unlike the well-studied repeating fast radio bursts from galaxy FRB-catalog source J0157+43, the NGC 5253-B signal has not been associated with any known host structure. The pulse train was first noticed in archival data collected over the past two years and only identified after the team developed a new signal-processing pipeline designed to detect faint, periodic sources. A similar candidate signal reported by a different team in 2021 near the same galaxy was later attributed to a satellite pass and retracted; the authors note their detection pipeline specifically flags and removes known satellite trajectories, though they acknowledge no such filter is perfect.

Listing Summary — 47 Chestnut Ridge Road, Millbrook. Price: $525,000 | 4 bed / 3 bath | 2,910 sq ft | Lot: 0.6 acres | Built: 2005.

This spacious colonial features an updated kitchen (2021), finished basement, and a two-car attached garage. The home is served by a private well and a septic system, both inspected in the past year. Seller is including the washer, dryer, and kitchen refrigerator in the sale. Showings by appointment only.

Inspection Report Summary (prepared by Redline Home Inspections, dated August 14): Overall, the home is in good condition for its age. The roof, installed in 2015, shows normal wear with an estimated remaining life of 8-10 years; no active leaks were observed. The HVAC system (installed 2005, original to the home) is functional but nearing the end of its typical service life; the inspector recommends budgeting for replacement within 3-5 years. The septic system was pumped and inspected on July 30 and passed with no deficiencies noted. Minor moisture staining was observed in one corner of the basement, consistent with a past event; no active water intrusion was detected during the inspection, which took place during a period of heavy rain. The electrical panel is a 200-amp service installed in 2005 and met code at installation; two circuits were found without proper labeling, a minor item. The inspector found no evidence of termite damage or active infestation, though he recommends a separate termite-specific inspection given the property's wooded lot, as this report does not substitute for one.

Seller's Disclosure Addendum: Seller discloses a basement water event in 2019 caused by a clogged exterior drain, which was repaired at the time; seller is not aware of any recurrence since the repair.

Agent notes: Buyer's financing is contingent on the termite inspection the buyer's agent has separately ordered for August 25.

Additional inspection notes: The water heater is a 50-gallon gas unit installed in 2016, functioning normally with no signs of corrosion. Attic insulation measures approximately R-38, consistent with current energy-code recommendations for the region. The garage door opener was tested and operates normally, including the safety reverse sensor.

Buyer's agent follow-up: The buyer asked whether the 2019 basement water event required an insurance claim; seller's agent responded that no claim was filed because the repair cost was under the policy deductible at the time. The seller's disclosure addendum notes the exterior drain was cleared and re-graded away from the foundation as part of the 2019 repair.

notes: Only past staining noted; no active intrusion despite heavy rain during inspection.

Meridian Industrial Holdings — Annual Report Excerpt, Segment Review.

Meridian Industrial Holdings operates through three reportable segments: Meridian Fabrication, Coreline Logistics, and Aspen Materials, the latter acquired in March of the reporting year.

Meridian Fabrication, the company's largest segment, generated revenue of $1.24 billion, roughly flat compared to $1.21 billion in the prior year. Segment operating margin declined to 11.2% from 13.5%, which management attributes to higher steel input costs that were only partially offset by price increases passed to customers.

Coreline Logistics revenue grew 18% to $640 million, driven by increased freight volumes and a new long-term contract with a major grocery chain that began in the second quarter. This segment's operating margin improved to 9.8% from 8.1%.

Aspen Materials, acquired for $310 million in an all-cash transaction, contributed $95 million in revenue during its nine months of ownership within the reporting year; on a pro forma full-year basis, management estimates Aspen would have contributed approximately $130 million. Aspen's results are not included in prior-year comparatives, as the acquisition had not yet closed.

Risk Factors (excerpt): The company notes that Meridian Fabrication's profitability is sensitive to steel and aluminum commodity prices, which the company does not hedge beyond short-term supplier contracts. The company also discloses an ongoing dispute with a former Coreline Logistics customer over contract termination fees, seeking damages of approximately $8 million; the company believes the claim is without merit and intends to contest it, but notes that litigation outcomes are inherently uncertain and an adverse ruling could result in a charge to earnings.

Total company revenue across all segments, including corporate eliminations of $14 million, was $1.965 billion for the reporting year, compared to $1.85 billion in the prior year.

The company's board approved a share repurchase program of up to $150 million, though as of the report date no shares had yet been repurchased under the new authorization.

Liquidity: As of the end of the reporting year, the company held $210 million in cash and cash equivalents and had $180 million available under its revolving credit facility, which matures in three years. Total long-term debt was $580 million, with a weighted average interest rate of 5.4%.

Outlook: Management expects Meridian Fabrication's margin pressure to ease gradually in the coming year as recently negotiated steel supply contracts take effect, though it cautions that commodity prices remain volatile and that no specific margin target is being provided at this time.

Initial Report (filed 2:15 p.m.): Bramwell Motors announced today it is recalling approximately 45,000 units of its 2024-2025 Voltra EV due to a software defect that could cause the parking brake to disengage unexpectedly on inclines steeper than 15 degrees. The company said owners would be notified by mail within two weeks and that a free over-the-air software update would resolve the issue for most vehicles; a small subset built before November 2024 will need an in-person dealer visit to replace a related sensor.

Correction (filed 5:40 p.m.): Bramwell Motors clarified that the recall affects approximately 38,000 units, not 45,000 as the company initially stated in its morning press release; the lower figure excludes about 7,000 vehicles that already received the corrected software during a routine update in March. A company spokesperson said the original figure was based on total production volume rather than the number of affected, unpatched vehicles. All other details of the recall, including the incline threshold and the in-person dealer visit requirement for pre-November 2024 vehicles, remain unchanged.

Separately, rival automaker Halden Auto said its own EV line uses a different parking-brake supplier and is not affected by this recall or any related issue.

Bramwell said no accidents or injuries have been linked to the defect so far, and that the issue was discovered internally during routine validation testing rather than through a customer complaint.

Meta-Analysis: Effect of Structured Exercise Programs on Post-Surgical Recovery Time.

We pooled data from 14 randomized trials (total n=2,340) examining whether structured post-operative exercise programs reduce time to independent mobility after elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Studies varied in exercise intensity, starting point (immediate post-op vs. 1 week post-op), and surgery type.

Pooled results showed that structured exercise programs reduced median time to independent mobility by 1.8 days (95% CI, 1.1-2.5 days) compared to standard care. The effect was larger for knee replacement patients (2.4 days) than hip replacement patients (1.2 days). Programs that began within 24 hours of surgery showed a larger benefit (2.6 days) than those starting after 1 week (0.9 days).

Heterogeneity across studies was moderate (I²=48%), and a funnel plot suggested some possible publication bias, meaning the true pooled effect could be somewhat smaller than reported. Only 3 of the 14 included trials were rated low risk of bias on all domains; the remaining 11 had at least one domain rated as unclear or high risk, most often around blinding of outcome assessors, which is inherently difficult in exercise interventions.

Two trials specifically examining shoulder replacement surgery were excluded from this analysis because shoulder recovery trajectories were judged too clinically different from hip and knee recovery to pool meaningfully; a separate review of shoulder-specific rehabilitation is planned.

No trials included in this analysis reported serious adverse events attributable to the exercise programs themselves, though 4 trials reported temporary increases in reported pain during the first week of the program, which resolved without intervention.

We conclude that structured exercise programs, particularly those started early, are associated with meaningfully faster return to independent mobility after hip or knee replacement, though the moderate heterogeneity and risk-of-bias concerns in most included trials warrant some caution in interpreting the magnitude of this effect.

A pre-specified sensitivity analysis excluding the three trials with the highest risk-of-bias ratings produced a similar pooled estimate (1.6 days, 95% CI 0.9-2.3), suggesting the overall result is not driven solely by lower-quality studies. Subgroup analysis by patient age (above vs. below 70 years) found no statistically significant difference in the size of the exercise benefit between age groups, though the youngest and oldest subgroups had wider confidence intervals due to smaller sample sizes within those strata. Cost data were reported in only 4 of the 14 trials and were not pooled due to substantial differences in how physical therapy visits were billed across health systems; a qualitative summary of those 4 trials suggested structured programs were cost-neutral to modestly cost-saving when accounting for reduced length of hospital stay, but the authors caution this finding is based on a small, non-representative subset of the pooled trials.

notes: 2.6 days vs 0.9 days.

state: Erratum to: 'Catalytic Efficiency of Compound X-14 in Nitrogen Fixation' (originally published March 2025). The original article reported a turnover frequency of 420 h⁻¹ for Compound X-14 under standard conditions. Following a re-analysis prompted by an independent lab's inability to replicate this figure, the authors identified a calibration error in the original gas chromatography measurements. The corrected turnover frequency is 168 h⁻¹, roughly 40% of the originally reported value. The authors state that this correction does not affect the paper's qualitative conclusion that Compound X-14 outperforms the previous benchmark catalyst, Compound W-9 (turnover frequency 110 h⁻¹), but does affect the magnitude of the reported improvement, which is now approximately 53% rather than the originally claimed 282%. The authors have also corrected Figure 3 and Table 2 accordingly and thank the independent lab for identifying the discrepancy.

Earnings Call Transcript Excerpt — Vantera Corp Q3 Results.

Operator: We'll now take questions. First question from Ellis Wong at Birchfield Securities.

Ellis Wong: Thanks. Can you talk about the gross margin decline this quarter and whether that's expected to continue?

CFO Rina Alsop: Sure, Ellis. Gross margin was 42%, down from 46% last quarter, primarily due to a one-time inventory write-down of $6 million related to a discontinued product line. Excluding that write-down, gross margin would have been approximately 45.5%, essentially flat sequentially. We don't expect the write-down to recur, so we'd expect margin to normalize back toward the mid-40s next quarter, though component costs remain a modest headwind.

Operator: Next question from Priya Anand at Oakstone Capital.

Priya Anand: On the guidance cut for full-year revenue, how much of that is the divested logistics unit versus organic softness?

CEO Daniel Fenwick: Good question, Priya. Of the $40 million reduction in our full-year guidance, about $30 million reflects the deconsolidation of the logistics unit we sold in August, and the remaining $10 million reflects modestly softer demand in our core enterprise segment, mainly in EMEA. We want to be clear that the divestiture is the larger factor by far.

Priya Anand: Understood. And is the $10 million softness something you expect to persist into next year?

Daniel Fenwick: Too early to say definitively, but the early read from our sales team is that it's more pipeline timing than lost deals, so we're cautiously optimistic it doesn't persist, though we're not baking that optimism into guidance yet.

Operator: Next question from Tomas Reyes at Fielding Asset Management.

Tomas Reyes: Quick one on capital allocation — with the logistics divestiture proceeds, are you planning any share buybacks?

CFO Rina Alsop: Thanks, Tomas. We received $85 million in net proceeds from the divestiture. Our priority is first paying down $25 million of higher-cost debt, and the board has approved a new $50 million buyback authorization for the remainder, though the pace of repurchases will depend on where the stock trades relative to our internal view of intrinsic value. We don't have a specific timeline to share beyond that.

Tomas Reyes: And is that $50 million incremental to the $20 million left on the prior authorization?

CFO Rina Alsop: Good catch — no, the new $50 million authorization replaces and supersedes the prior one; the $20 million remaining under the old authorization is no longer available separately.

Operator: That concludes our Q&A session.

state: Material Restatement Notice: Calloway Foods Inc. announced it will restate its financial statements for fiscal years 2023 and 2024 after identifying an error in how it recognized revenue from long-term co-packing agreements. The company previously recognized revenue upfront upon contract signing; under the correct accounting treatment, revenue should be recognized ratably over the life of each agreement. The restatement is expected to reduce previously reported FY2023 revenue by approximately $14 million and FY2024 revenue by approximately $9 million, with a corresponding increase in revenue recognized in later periods as those contracts continue. The company stated the error does not affect historical cash flows or the total contract value of any agreement, only the timing of when revenue was recognized in the financial statements. The audit committee has concluded the error was unintentional and related to a misapplication of a new accounting standard adopted in early 2023, not to any fraudulent activity. The company's previously issued financial statements for FY2023 and FY2024 should no longer be relied upon.

To: support@nexoria.com
Subject: Laptop shuts down randomly

Hi, my Nexoria Slate 14 has been shutting down on its own several times a day, usually when it gets warm on my lap. Getting worried it will damage something.

-- Reply from Support (Agent Tia) --
Sorry to hear that, David. Could you send us the serial number from the bottom panel so we can check the warranty status?

-- Reply from David --
Serial number is NX14-88213-B. Also meant to mention, the trackpad has started double-clicking when I only click once, started around the same time as the shutdowns.

-- Reply from Agent Tia --
Thanks David, I've confirmed NX14-88213-B is still within its 1-year warranty (purchased about 4 months ago). Given the combination of shutdowns and a new trackpad fault, I'd like to rule out a loose internal connection before we jump to a full repair. Could you try two things: (1) boot into Safe Mode and see if the shutdowns still happen, and (2) run the built-in hardware diagnostic from the boot menu (hold F10 at startup) and send us the report code it gives you.

-- Reply from David --
Ran the diagnostic, it gave code TH-204, which the on-screen text labeled a thermal sensor fault. Safe Mode ran fine for about 40 minutes without shutting down, but the trackpad double-click issue happened even in Safe Mode, so that seems unrelated to the shutdowns.

-- Reply from Agent Tia --
That's helpful, thank you. TH-204 confirms a faulty thermal sensor, which explains the shutdowns and is a covered hardware repair. The trackpad issue looks like a separate fault and is also covered. I'm issuing a prepaid shipping label for a depot repair -- turnaround is typically 5-7 business days once we receive the unit. Understood, that works. One last thing -- will the repair wipe my hard drive? I haven't backed up in a while.

Good question -- our standard motherboard and sensor repairs don't touch the drive, but we always recommend backing up beforehand just in case, since a small percentage of repairs do end up requiring a drive swap.

state:
TV PANEL DEFECT & DAMAGE POLICY (rev. 4)
1. Standard warranty: any television with 5 or more dead or stuck pixels found within 90 days of delivery qualifies for a free replacement panel or unit, no deductible.
2. After 90 days from delivery, dead-pixel claims are not covered under the standard warranty regardless of pixel count.
3. Extended Care Plan (if purchased at checkout): extends dead-pixel coverage to 365 days from delivery, subject to the same 5-pixel threshold, no deductible. The Extended Care Plan does NOT cover cosmetic scratches or user-caused cracks.
4. Accidental damage (drops, cracks) is covered only under the separate Accidental Damage Add-on, subject to a $150 deductible, maximum 2 claims per year.
5. Priority order: if a unit qualifies under both the standard warranty and the Extended Care Plan, apply the standard warranty first (no deductible either way, but avoids drawing down the Extended Care claim count).
6. Registration requirement: the Extended Care Plan is only active if the customer registers the plan within 14 days of the delivery date, via the online portal or by calling support. Claims filed under an unregistered Extended Care Plan are treated as if no Extended Care Plan had been purchased at all.

CASE FILE
Customer: Bram Voss
Product: Nexoria 55in OLED
Purchase date: Jan 3
Delivery date: Jan 10
Extended Care Plan: purchased at checkout, registered online on Jan 12
Accidental Damage Add-on: not purchased
Today's date: Apr 20 (100 days after delivery)
Reported issue: 6 dead pixels clustered in the lower-left corner. No drops, cracks, or physical damage reported or observed by the technician.

Technician visit note, Apr 18: Confirmed 6 dead/stuck pixels in the lower-left quadrant using a full-screen color test pattern. Panel otherwise structurally intact; no cracks, dents, or liquid ingress observed. Customer stated the pixels appeared gradually over the past two weeks, not from a single incident.

Customer's original complaint, submitted via the support portal on Apr 19: "I've noticed a cluster of dead pixels on my TV, seems to have appeared over the last couple of weeks. This is my first time dealing with this, what are my options? I did buy the Extended Care add-on so I'm hoping that's still valid even though it's past the 3-month mark."

Claim reference: WC-2291. Logged by Support Agent Priya N. Escalation required: no, standard Extended Care workflow applies. Customer account notes: this is the first warranty claim on file for this account, with no prior claims history.

state:
Support chat transcript - Case #77410
Customer: The battery on my Pixelwave Aero drone drops from 100% to 20% in about 6 minutes of flight, way below the advertised 25 minute flight time.
Agent Sana: Sorry for the trouble! Can you try a full battery calibration cycle -- drain it completely, then charge uninterrupted for 4 hours?
Customer: Already tried that twice this week, no change at all, still drops the same way.
Agent Sana: Understood, that rules out a calibration issue. Can you tell me your firmware version? Settings > About > Firmware.
Customer: It says v2.3.1.
Agent Sana: Thanks, we've had a few reports of a battery-reporting bug on v2.3.1 specifically, engineering is treating it as a confirmed firmware defect. Since this is a manufacturing/firmware defect rather than misuse, I can send a replacement battery at no charge, and we'll cover return shipping for the old one.
Customer: That works, thank you. Just to confirm, I don't pay anything for the return shipping label?
Agent Sana: Correct, zero cost to you -- we email a prepaid label since this is a confirmed defect.
Customer: Great, appreciate it. While I have you -- my other drone, a Pixelwave Mini, has developed a propeller wobble on takeoff, totally different unit. Can you help with that here too?
Agent Sana: I'd like to help, but that's a different product and a different issue, so I'll need to open a separate case for the Mini rather than handling it under Case #77410. I'll send a new chat link so the two repairs don't get mixed up.
Customer: Fair enough, I'll start a new chat for that one. For this case, how will I know when the replacement battery ships?
Agent Sana: You'll get an automatic email with tracking as soon as the warehouse packs it, usually within 1-2 business days from now. The prepaid return label for your old battery is already in a separate email in your inbox.
Customer: Got it, thank you for sorting this out so quickly.
Agent Sana: Happy to help! Anything else I can do for you on Case #77410 specifically?
Customer: No, that covers it for this one.

[Chat ended 16:47. Case #77410 status: replacement battery approved, awaiting warehouse fulfillment. Agent Sana's shift note: firmware v2.3.1 battery-reporting defect flagged for engineering review across the affected production batch; no further action needed from this particular customer at this time.]

state:
FORMAL NOTICE OF DEFECTIVE GOODS

Date: 14 March
To: Clarion Retail Customer Rights Department
Re: Order #CR-40218, Clarion Vista 27in Monitor. Purchased 24 February for $612.00 including tax via credit card; delivered 1 March; invoice #INV-77821.

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing pursuant to Section 54 of the Consumer Guarantees Act regarding the above order. Upon unboxing on 1 March, the monitor's screen was found to be cracked across the lower third. The shipping carton and internal foam packaging showed no dents, tears, or signs of impact, which indicates the panel most likely left the factory already cracked rather than being damaged in transit.

This is my second attempt to raise this matter. I first called your support line on 4 March (reference CS-88213) and was told a case manager would call back within 48 hours; no call was received. I called again on 9 March and was told the case had been closed in error without ever contacting me.

For the avoidance of doubt, I have attached to this letter (Appendix A) four photographs of the crack taken in natural light, along with a photograph of the intact packaging materials referenced above. I also took the unit to an independent repair shop, GreenTech Repairs, on 6 March for a second opinion; their technician, without prompting, independently concluded the crack pattern was consistent with a factory-applied panel defect rather than an impact fracture.

For context, this is the second Clarion product I have purchased this year; the first, a Clarion SoundBar Mini, has performed without any issues, so I do not believe I am simply having bad luck with this brand.

I request a full replacement unit under Section 54(2) of the Act. I am not seeking a monetary refund at this time, as I would like to continue using this monitor model. Under Section 55 of the Act, retailers are required to substantively respond to a written defect notice within 10 business days of receipt; I therefore expect a response by 28 March. If the matter remains unresolved by that date, I will file a complaint with the Consumer Disputes Tribunal and will seek reimbursement of my call costs in addition to the replacement.

Please advise on return logistics for the defective unit at your earliest convenience. This letter is sent without prejudice to any other statutory rights I may have.

Regards,
Elena Kovac

CC: Consumer Rights Advocacy Group (information only)
Enclosures: Appendix A (four photographs), GreenTech Repairs assessment note

1. Account deletion requests are processed within 30 calendar days of the request date. During this window, the account is in a 'pending deletion' state: data is inaccessible to the user but not yet purged.
2. A pending deletion can be reversed if the user contacts support and explicitly requests reactivation before the 30-day window closes. After the window closes, deletion is permanent and irreversible.
3. Billing: any active subscription is cancelled immediately upon submission of a deletion request; no partial-period refund is issued for the remainder of a paid term, per the Terms of Service.
4. Business/Team accounts: deletion of a Team account requires confirmation from the account owner, not just any team member, and follows the same 30-day window once confirmed by the owner.
5. Legal holds: if an account is subject to a legal hold (e.g., active litigation, regulatory request), deletion is suspended until the hold is lifted, regardless of the 30-day window.
6. Communication: deletion-related confirmations (including reactivation requests) must be made through the account's registered email or the in-app support chat. A phone call alone can initiate a discussion but is not sufficient to action a reversal; a written request is always required.

SUPPORT CASE LOG
Account: personal plan, owner Naledi Mokoena
Deletion requested: Mar 1
Today's date: Mar 26 (25 days after the request)
Legal hold: none on file
Account type: personal (not a Team account)

Phone log, Mar 20: Naledi called in and verbally asked about reactivating, but was told a written request (email or chat) would be required to action it, per clause 6; no written request followed at that time.

Mar 24 message from Naledi (submitted via in-app chat): "Hi, I changed my mind, please reactivate my account, I still need the files in there for a work project."

Unrelated note on file: Naledi is also a member (not owner) of a separate Corvus Cloud Team account (ID T-2291) belonging to her employer; that Team account is not part of this deletion request and remains fully active throughout.

Agent note, Mar 26: Confirmed no legal hold. Confirmed the Mar 24 in-app chat message is a valid written request under clause 6, and falls within the 30-day pending-deletion window (day 25 of 30, counting from the Mar 1 request). Proceeding to reverse the deletion and restore full account access. No refund is owed for the subscription period that was already cancelled on Mar 1, per clause 3.

Pause the request pending a legal hold

From: it-procurement@larkspurlaw.com
To: accounts@meridiancrm.com
Date: Sept 10
Subject: Meridian CRM renewal - 40 seats

Our annual Meridian CRM license for 40 seats renews on Sept 30. We're considering adding 15 more seats at renewal, bringing us to 55 total. Your published pricing page shows a 20% discount tier starting at 50 seats. Can you confirm the 55-seat renewal would qualify for that tier, and send a quote before Sept 30 so we can get budget approval in time? If we don't hear back by Sept 24, we may need to renew at just the current 40 seats without the expansion, since our budget cycle closes Sept 25.

-- Reply from Meridian Sales (Dara) --
Thanks for reaching out! Confirming our seat-based volume pricing: 1-19 seats is list price, 20-49 seats gets 10% off, 50-99 seats gets 20% off, and 100+ seats gets 25% off. At 55 seats you'd land in the 50-99 bracket, so the 20% tier applies to all 55 seats, not just the new 15. I've attached a formal quote reflecting 55 seats at 20% off, valid through Sept 24 to line up with your budget deadline. Separately, I wanted to flag that your current contract's auto-renewal clause means that if we don't hear back by Sept 30, it renews automatically at the existing 40 seats and current, non-discounted rate.

-- Reply from procurement --
Understood on the auto-renewal fallback. We'll aim to get you a decision by Sept 24 as planned. One more question: does the 20% tier apply retroactively if we renew at 40 seats now and add the other 15 later, in October, instead of at renewal?

-- Reply from Dara --
Good question -- no, the tier is evaluated at the time of the seat change, not retroactively. If you renew at 40 seats now and add 15 later, that later change would be evaluated on its own at that time rather than applying the 20% tier back to the whole account from the renewal date.

-- Reply from procurement --
Got it, that makes sense. Please go ahead and send the 55-seat quote to me and also CC our finance director, Owen Ferris, at o.ferris@larkspurlaw.com so he can start the approval process in parallel. We'll confirm one way or the other before the 24th.

-- Reply from Dara --
Done, quote sent to both of you just now, valid through Sept 24 as discussed. Looking forward to hearing back either way.

question.instruction: Does the customer state a firm deadline by which they need a response to include the seat expansion?

notes: States they need to hear back by Sept 24 due to their budget cycle closing Sept 25.

Your published pricing page shows a 20% discount tier starting at 50 seats. Can you confirm the 55-seat renewal would qualify for that tier, and send a quote before Sept 30 so we can get budget approval in time? If we don't hear back by Sept 24, we may need to renew at just the current 40 seats without the expansion, since our budget cycle closes Sept 25.

-- Reply from Meridian Sales (Dara) --
Thanks for reaching out! Confirming our seat-based volume pricing: 1-19 seats is list price, 20-49 seats gets 10% off, 50-99 seats gets 20% off, and 100+ seats gets 25% off. At 55 seats you'd land in the 50-99 bracket, so the 20% tier applies to all 55 seats, not just the new 15. I've attached a formal quote reflecting 55 seats at 20% off, valid through Sept 24 to line up with your budget deadline. Separately, I wanted to flag that your current contract's auto-renewal clause means that if we don't hear back by Sept 30, it renews automatically at the existing 40 seats and current, non-discounted rate.

-- Reply from procurement --
Understood on the auto-renewal fallback. We'll aim to get you a decision by Sept 24 as planned. One more question: does the 20% tier apply retroactively if we renew at 40 seats now and add the other 15 later, in October, instead of at renewal?

-- Reply from Dara --
Good question -- no, the tier is evaluated at the time of the seat change, not retroactively. If you renew at 40 seats now and add 15 later, that later change would be evaluated on its own at that time rather than applying the 20% tier back to the whole account from the renewal date.

-- Reply from procurement --
Got it, that makes sense. Please go ahead and send the 55-seat quote to me and also CC our finance director, Owen Ferris, at o.ferris@larkspurlaw.com so he can start the approval process in parallel. We'll confirm one way or the other before the 24th.

-- Reply from Dara --
Done, quote sent to both of you just now, valid through Sept 24 as discussed. Looking forward to hearing back either way.

INCIDENT REPORT #IR-2091 -- Cascade Foods Processing Plant, Line 4
Date of incident: 2026-02-11 | Reported by: T. Alvarez, Shift Supervisor

At approximately 14:20, contractor Ben Okafor (employed by Meridian Maintenance Services, not a Cascade Foods employee) was performing scheduled lubrication on the conveyor gearbox on Line 4 when his sleeve caught in an unguarded pinch point. Okafor sustained a laceration to his right forearm requiring 6 stitches at Riverside Urgent Care. He returned to modified duty the same day and did not miss any scheduled shifts. The machine guard for this gearbox had been removed two weeks prior for a bearing replacement and was not reinstalled -- this has been logged as a contributing factor. No Cascade Foods employees were involved in the direct incident, though Line 4 operator M. Kwan witnessed the event and shut down the line immediately.

No chemical exposure occurred. No fire or explosion. The area was dry; this was not a slip/fall incident. PPE (cut-resistant sleeves) was available in the tool crib but was not being worn at the time.

---
From: T. Alvarez
To: safety@cascadefoods.example
Subject: Re: IR-2091 follow-up
Date: 2026-02-12

Hi team, per our call: the missing guard is the root cause. Maintenance has been told to reinstall guards immediately after any service, no exceptions. I've also asked Meridian to confirm their techs are briefed on our PPE rules -- sounds like that briefing didn't happen for Okafor's crew this month.

---
From: D. Ferris, EHS Manager
To: T. Alvarez
Subject: Re: IR-2091 follow-up
Date: 2026-02-13

Agreed. For classification purposes: since Okafor works for Meridian and received treatment beyond first aid (sutures), I'm logging this as a recordable third-party contractor injury on our OSHA-300A-equivalent contractor log, not on Cascade Foods' own employee injury log. It does not count as a Cascade Foods lost-time case since he didn't lose any of his own scheduled shifts with us -- and he's not our employee to begin with. Corrective action (guard reinstallation SOP) is still open, due 2026-02-28.

---
From: Priya Nandakumar, Corporate EHS Director
To: D. Ferris
Subject: Re: IR-2091 follow-up
Date: 2026-02-16

Thanks for the writeup. For our quarterly trending report, can you confirm this is the only pinch-point guarding incident at the Cascade Foods plant level (not just Line 4) in the past 6 months? I want to make sure we're not missing a pattern across other lines before I present to the safety committee next week.

---
From: D. Ferris
To: Priya Nandakumar
Date: 2026-02-16

Confirmed, this is the only guarding-related incident plant-wide in the past 6 months. Lines 1-3 and 5-6 have no similar findings in that window. I'll have the full trending report to you by Friday.

Vendor Security Assessment Call -- Transcript excerpt
Participants: Ingrid Solberg (Customer, Security Team), Felix Ngata (Anchorpoint Cyber, Solutions Engineer)
Date: 2026-07-14

Solberg: Let's go through our checklist. First, data residency -- can you guarantee our data stays in the US?
Ngata: For our Standard tier, no -- data may be processed in our US or EU regions depending on load balancing. For the Enterprise tier, yes, we offer a US-only data residency commitment, contractually guaranteed.
Solberg: We'd be on Enterprise. Good. Encryption?
Ngata: Everything is encrypted at rest with AES-256, and in transit with TLS 1.3. That's true across all tiers.
Solberg: Background checks on your engineering staff?
Ngata: Yes, all employees with production access go through a background check as part of onboarding, regardless of tier.
Solberg: SOC 2?
Ngata: We hold SOC 2 Type I, completed last year. We have not yet completed Type II -- that audit is scheduled to start in Q4 2026, results expected mid-2027.
Solberg: Okay, noted as not yet held. Incident response -- what's your SLA for notifying us of a breach?
Ngata: Contractually, 48 hours from confirmed breach for Enterprise customers. For Standard tier it's best-effort with no contractual SLA.
Solberg: And do you carry cyber insurance?
Ngata: Yes, we carry a $5M cyber liability policy.
Solberg: Great. Multi-factor authentication for customer-facing accounts?
Ngata: MFA is available but optional for end users on Standard tier. On Enterprise tier we can enforce it org-wide if you want -- it's off by default until you ask us to turn it on.
Solberg: We'll definitely want that turned on, but as of today it's not on unless we request it, correct?
Ngata: Correct, nothing is turned on automatically -- you'd submit a config request post-contract.
Solberg: Understood. Subprocessors?
Ngata: We maintain a public subprocessor list and notify customers 30 days in advance of adding a new one, with a right to object.
Solberg: One more -- penetration testing?
Ngata: Annual third-party pentest, yes. Last one was March 2026, next one is scheduled March 2027.

[Internal note from Solberg to her manager, forwarded separately: 'Overall solid. Two gaps for our Enterprise contract to close explicitly: SOC 2 Type II isn't done yet, and MFA enforcement needs to be requested -- it won't just happen.']

Solberg: Last thing -- how long are audit logs retained?
Ngata: 18 months by default for Enterprise tier, 90 days for Standard tier -- that's independent of the MFA and residency settings we discussed.
Solberg: Good to know, noted for our records.

Article 3 - Insurance. Contractor shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence and workers' compensation insurance as required by state law. Client shall be named as an additional insured. Contractor shall provide certificates of insurance annually.

Article 4 - Personnel. All guards assigned to Client's premises must pass a criminal background check and a drug screen prior to assignment. Contractor may not subcontract any portion of the guard services to a third-party security firm without Client's prior written consent; general support services (payroll, scheduling software) are not considered subcontracted guard services and do not require consent.

Article 5 - Exclusivity. This Agreement is non-exclusive. Client may engage other security vendors for other locations or shifts at its sole discretion. Contractor may also serve other clients, including, for the avoidance of doubt, other law firms, provided no conflict of interest arises with respect to Client's specific matters.

Article 6 - Pricing. The hourly bill rate is fixed at $34/hour for the first 12 months. Thereafter, Contractor may increase rates once per calendar year with 60 days' written notice, capped at the greater of 4% or the change in the regional CPI.

Article 7 - Liability. Contractor's aggregate liability for any claim is limited to $1,000,000 or the fees paid in the preceding 6 months, whichever is greater. This cap does not apply to claims arising from Contractor's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of the background-check requirement in Article 4.

Article 8 - Termination. Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience with 30 days' written notice. Contractor may not terminate for convenience during the first 12 months of the Term; after 12 months, Contractor may terminate for convenience with 90 days' notice.

Article 9 - Non-Solicitation. Neither party will solicit the other's employees for hire during the Term. This Agreement contains no non-compete restricting either party's ability to operate in the same market generally.

Article 10 - Arbitration. Any dispute shall be resolved in the state courts of the Agreement's governing state; this Agreement does not include an arbitration clause, and either party retains the right to a jury trial.

Article 11 - Data. Contractor does not process Client's client-confidential legal files; guards have no access to Client's document management systems. No Data Processing Addendum is included or needed under this Agreement.

Site Safety Incident Report -- Ironclad Construction Co., 4th & Vine Tower Project
Date: 2026-03-22 | Filed by: Site Safety Officer Yusuf Karimi

At 09:40, apprentice electrician Delphine Aubert (Ironclad employee, 3 months on the job) received an electrical shock while working on a junction box she believed was de-energized. Lockout/tagout tags were in place, but a subcontractor from a separate trade had temporarily re-energized the adjacent circuit for testing without communicating with the electrical crew -- a lockout/tagout communication failure. Aubert was transported to St. Mary's Hospital as a precaution, evaluated, and released the same day with no burns or lasting injury; she did not return to the site for the remainder of her shift but was cleared to return the next day.

No other workers were affected. No fall, no fire. This is the second LOTO-communication incident on this site in 4 months; the first (2025-11-30) involved a different subcontractor and no injury.

Site Safety Officer recommendation: Given the injury requiring hospital evaluation and the missed remainder-of-shift, this meets our internal threshold for a recordable lost-time case. Escalating to corporate EHS for OSHA recordability determination and mandatory LOTO refresher training for all site subcontractors within 10 days.

INCIDENT REPORT -- Basalt Ridge Mining Co., Processing Building 2
Date: 2026-05-09 | Filed by: Naledi Dube, Site EHS Coordinator

At 13:05, an electrical panel in the west switchgear room began smoking after a breaker fault. The building fire alarm activated automatically and all 34 personnel on shift (28 Basalt Ridge employees, 6 contractors from Ridgeline Structural Engineering performing unrelated structural inspections) evacuated via the marked routes within 4 minutes, per the muster point log. The in-panel fire suppression system (FM-200) discharged automatically and extinguished the fire before it spread beyond the panel enclosure. The local fire department was called as a precaution and cleared the building at 13:45; no fire department suppression action was needed. No injuries were reported among employees or contractors. Building 2 was closed for the remainder of the shift while an electrician assessed the panel; production resumed the next morning.

---
From: Naledi Dube
To: ehs-leadership@basaltridge.example
Subject: Building 2 electrical incident - initial notes
Date: 2026-05-09

Quick update before the full report: everyone's accounted for and safe. Muster took 4 minutes, within our target. FM-200 did exactly what it's supposed to do. If that suppression system had failed to discharge, we could have been looking at a much bigger fire and possible injuries during evacuation -- but that's not what happened here, thankfully. I'll have root cause from the electrician by Friday.

---
From: Colton Baird, VP Operations
To: Naledi Dube
Date: 2026-05-09

Good work getting everyone out fast. For the record, since the Ridgeline contractors were on-site during a Basalt Ridge safety event, do we need to loop in their safety office?

---
From: Naledi Dube
To: Colton Baird
Date: 2026-05-09

Yes, I've already notified Ridgeline's site supervisor since their personnel were present for the evacuation, even though none of them were injured and the incident originated in our equipment, not theirs. Standard practice per our site access agreement.

---
From: Colton Baird
To: Naledi Dube
Date: 2026-05-10

Did Ridgeline's site supervisor have any concerns on their end?

---
From: Naledi Dube
To: Colton Baird
Date: 2026-05-10

No concerns raised. Their supervisor confirmed all 6 of their people were accounted for at muster and none required any medical attention. They asked to be copied on our final root-cause report once the electrician finishes the assessment, which I've agreed to.

---
From: Naledi Dube
To: ehs-leadership@basaltridge.example
Subject: Re: Building 2 electrical incident - root cause
Date: 2026-05-15

Root cause confirmed: a loose lug connection on the breaker caused arcing and localized overheating. Electrician has re-torqued all connections in the panel and performed thermal imaging on the rest of the switchgear room; no other hot spots found. Building 2 is cleared to resume normal two-shift operation starting tomorrow.

Calloway Biotech Foundation -- Translational Research Award -- Full Program Guidelines (excerpt)

1. Purpose. This award supports late-stage preclinical research with a clear path to clinical translation within 5 years.

2. Eligibility. Applicant must be a faculty member (Assistant Professor or above) at a degree-granting research institution. Postdocs and graduate students may not apply as Principal Investigator but may be named as Co-Investigators. There is no citizenship or nationality requirement -- the PI may be a citizen of any country, provided the host institution is accredited and the funds are administered through that institution's sponsored programs office.

3. Preliminary Data. Applicants MUST include preliminary data supporting feasibility; applications without any preliminary data will be returned without review, no exceptions.

4. Budget. Awards up to $400,000 over 2 years. Equipment purchases over $25,000 require separate pre-approval from the Foundation before the proposal is submitted, not after award.

5. Human/Animal Subjects. If applicable, IACUC or IRB approval must be in place (not just pending) at the time of submission -- this differs from many federal programs that allow pending approval.

6. Industry Partnership. A letter of support from an industry partner is optional and does not affect scoring, contrary to a rumor circulating in some departments; the Foundation does not weigh industry letters in review at all.

7. Reporting. Semiannual progress reports are required throughout the award period. A no-cost extension of up to 6 months may be requested once, at least 60 days before the original end date.

8. Renewal. This award is not renewable; awardees may apply to a future cycle with a new, substantially different project, but not a continuation of the same aims.

9. Publication. Awardees are encouraged, but not required, to acknowledge Calloway Biotech Foundation support in resulting publications.

Halcyon SaaS Suite -- Data Handling & Offboarding Policy (shared with Ridgeline Structural Engineering during procurement, 2026-03-18)

Data retention: Active account data is retained for the life of the subscription. Upon cancellation, data is retained in a read-only archive state for 30 days, then permanently deleted. Customers may request an export of their data in CSV/JSON format at any time during the subscription or within the 30-day post-cancellation window; exports are not available after permanent deletion.

Deletion requests: Customers may request immediate permanent deletion (bypassing the 30-day archive) via a signed request to legal@halcyon.example; standard processing time is 10 business days.

Backups: Encrypted backups are retained for an additional 35 days beyond the primary deletion for disaster-recovery purposes only, and are not accessible for routine export -- they exist solely to restore service in case of a platform-wide failure, not for individual customer data recovery requests.

Subprocessor access: Our backup storage subprocessor (Glacier Vault Inc.) has encrypted-at-rest access only and no application-level access to readable customer data.

Lab Safety Incident Report -- Fernbridge Research Institute, Chemistry Building Room 214
Date: 2026-04-05 | Filed by: Lab Safety Officer Junko Ishikawa

Graduate student Callan Reyes was transferring approximately 200mL of a dilute hydrochloric acid solution between containers in the fume hood when a cracked flask leaked onto the fume hood work surface. Reyes was wearing the required goggles, gloves, and lab coat; no skin or eye contact occurred. The spill was fully contained within the fume hood and neutralized with the on-shelf spill kit within 5 minutes. No evacuation was necessary. Principal Investigator Dr. Wilhelmina Voss was not present in the lab at the time; she was notified by phone and returned within the hour to review the incident with Reyes.

Reyes noted in the incident interview: 'If I'd been transferring that outside the fume hood like I sometimes see people do in other labs, this could have been a much bigger deal with fumes everywhere -- but our SOP requires fume hood use for all acid transfers over 50mL, and I followed it.'

No injuries. Equipment: the cracked flask has been removed from the lab's glassware inventory. This is the second reported flask-cracking incident in this lab in 6 months; both involved older glassware from the same 2019 batch, which is now flagged for inspection.

Third-Party Security Audit Summary -- prepared by Blackthorn Cyber Defense for Quillfeather Publishing
Subject: Emberlight Analytics (SaaS analytics platform)
Audit date: 2026-05-20

1. Access Controls: Role-based access control (RBAC) is implemented; however, we found that 12 of 340 user accounts (3.5%) had not had their access reviewed in over 12 months, exceeding Emberlight's own stated 6-month review policy. MFA is enforced org-wide for all accounts, which meets requirements.

2. Encryption: Data at rest uses AES-256; data in transit uses TLS 1.2 (not the more current TLS 1.3, which Emberlight has on its roadmap for 2027).

3. Vulnerability Management: Emberlight patches critical vulnerabilities within 15 days on average, within their SLA of 30 days. However, we identified one critical vulnerability (CVE-2025-41102) that had been open for 52 days at the time of our audit, exceeding their own SLA -- Emberlight acknowledged this was an oversight during a staffing transition and has since patched it.

4. Logging & Monitoring: Centralized logging is in place with 13 months of retention, exceeding the 12-month minimum we require. Real-time alerting is configured for privileged account actions.

5. Incident History: Emberlight disclosed one prior security incident (2025-03), a misconfigured storage bucket that briefly exposed non-sensitive metadata (no customer content) for approximately 4 hours before detection and remediation. No customer data was confirmed compromised.

6. Subprocessors: All 5 subprocessors are disclosed with data flow diagrams; none are located outside the customer's selected data region.

7. Certifications: SOC 2 Type II (current, expires 2027-01), ISO 27001 (current, expires 2026-11).

Overall Finding: Emberlight substantially meets our security bar. Two findings require remediation before we can recommend full approval: (a) the stale access reviews for 12 accounts, and (b) documented process improvement for vulnerability SLA adherence given the CVE-2025-41102 lapse. Neither finding is severe enough to recommend against proceeding with a contract, provided remediation commitments are obtained in writing.

8. Contractual Terms Reviewed: We reviewed the draft Master Services Agreement's data protection addendum; terms are standard and include a 72-hour breach notification obligation consistent with Section 5's SLA commitments elsewhere in Emberlight's customer contracts.

---
Follow-up email, 2026-05-27:
From: Emberlight Security Team
To: Blackthorn Cyber Defense
Subject: Re: Audit findings remediation

Thank you for the summary. We commit to completing the overdue access reviews for all 12 flagged accounts by 2026-06-10, and to publishing an internal post-mortem on the CVE-2025-41102 SLA lapse, including process changes, by 2026-06-15. We'll provide evidence of both to Quillfeather's security team once complete.

Windrose Underwriters Community Resilience Fund -- 2026 Infrastructure Hardening Grants -- Full Guidelines

1. Eligibility. Open to municipal governments and special districts (water, fire, levee districts) in coastal and flood-prone counties as designated on the attached FEMA-derived map (Appendix A). Private property owners and homeowners associations are not eligible; they may benefit indirectly from publicly-owned infrastructure projects but cannot be the applicant of record.

2. Award Tiers and Match. Tier A (population under 10,000): awards up to $500,000, local match of 10%. Tier B (population 10,000-50,000): awards up to $2,000,000, local match of 15%. Tier C (population over 50,000): awards up to $5,000,000, local match of 25%. Match may include prior-approved state grants but not other Windrose Underwriters funding.

3. Eligible Projects. Seawalls, levee reinforcement, stormwater pump stations, and elevation of critical facilities (fire stations, water treatment plants). Projects must have a completed engineering feasibility study before applying -- a feasibility study in progress at the time of application is not sufficient.

4. Ineligible Costs. Routine maintenance of existing infrastructure is not fundable; this program funds hardening and resilience upgrades only, not deferred maintenance. Land acquisition costs are eligible only if the land is required for the specific hardening project (e.g., pump station siting), not for general municipal land banking.

5. Timeline. Applications open 2026-09-01, close 2026-12-15. Awards announced by 2027-03-01. Projects must begin construction within 12 months of award or the award may be rescinded.

6. Reporting. Quarterly progress reports during construction; a final engineering completion certification is required, not merely a financial closeout report.

7. Public Records. All awarded project files, including engineering certifications, become subject to public records requests once the award is finalized, consistent with standard municipal transparency law in this state.

---
